messages.content: my aunt keeps asking if i want another cup of tea. i liked the first one, but i do not want more. what can i say?
thank you. the tea was nice, but i do not want another cup.
i do not want her to think i did not like it.
you can keep both parts clear: you enjoyed the tea, and you have had enough for now.
write that as something i can say, not as an explanation.
i enjoyed the tea. thank you, but i have had enough for now.
she says there is more tea in the pot.
having more tea ready does not mean you have to drink more. you can thank her again and keep the same choice.
can i say maybe later if i do not know whether i will want it later?
yes, if later really is possible for you. but you do not need to choose another time just to make your no kind.
give me that answer more simply.
you can say no in a kind way without choosing another time to drink tea.
now i do want water. does that mean my first answer about tea was false?
no. you can want water without a wish for another cup of tea.
write one sentence that thanks her and asks for water instead.
thank you for the tea, but could i have some water now?
will that make clear i did not like the tea?
no. it asks for a different drink. it does not say you did not like the tea.
here are two sentences: the children went to their grandmother house. their mother stayed home. can you fix the first one without adding a new person?
the children went to the house of their grandmother.
now join the two sentences with while.
the children went to the house of their grandmother while their mother stayed home.
does while mean the mother stayed home because she was sad?
no. while can put the two things in the same part of the day. it does not give a reason or a feeling by itself.
what if i add she wanted to finish a book?
then you have given a possible reason for her being home. you can say she stayed home because she wanted to finish a book.
write the whole idea in two sentences.
the children went to the house of their grandmother while their mother stayed home. she wanted to finish a book.
who is she in your last sentence?
in that short story, she is their mother.
now write the story as if i am one of the children.
we went to the house of our grandmother while our mother stayed home. she wanted to finish a book.
can their mother still be right if i am one of the children?
it could mean the mother of some other people. if you mean your own mother and the mother of the other children in your group, our mother is more clear.
only give the first part about where we went.
we went to the house of our grandmother.
tell a story about a boy who thinks a plant is gone because it is no longer by the door. the plant should still be in the house.

a boy came home from school and looked by the front door. the plant that usually stood there was gone. he asked his father whether someone had taken it away. his father said to look in the living room. the boy went inside and found the plant near the window. his father explained that the place by the door had become too cold for it. the boy stood by the window and looked at the plant for a moment. then he went back to put his books away, knowing where to find it next time.
was the plant outside when he came home?
no. it was in the living room near the window.
why did he think it might be gone?
he did not see it in the place where it usually stood.
what did his father say was wrong with the old place?
it had become too cold for the plant.
can you tell me every plant should be kept near a window from that story?
no. the story is about this plant and this change of place. it does not give a rule for every plant.
write just the part where he finds it, in his own voice.
i went into the living room and found the plant near the window.
now change went to go and found to find so it sounds like a story happening now.
i go into the living room and find the plant near the window.
does that change which room the plant is in?
no. the room is still the living room. you changed the way the story gives the time of what happens.
make the last answer shorter.
no. the plant is in the same room in both sentences.
i want to walk to the park, but the road i usually use is closed. i know another road, though it takes longer.
then you can choose between taking the longer road and changing the visit. how much free time do you have?
i have an hour before i need to be home. i do not know how long the other walk takes.
then you do not yet know whether it works for that hour. could you check the walk time before leaving, or choose a place near home today?
what if i cannot check the walk time?
you could choose a place near home today if you cannot check whether the longer walk leaves enough time to return.
my friend has walked that way and says it takes ten minutes to the park.
if that is right for your walk, you would need ten minutes to get there and ten to come home. you also need to leave time for the visit itself.
does that leave any time for the park before i need to be home?
you would need ten minutes to get there and ten to come home. that leaves part of your hour for the park, if nothing else changes.
do i have to stay the whole rest of the hour?
no. you can leave before the whole hour is gone and give yourself more time to get home if the walk takes longer than you think.
give me the reason for leaving some time open.
you can leave before the whole hour is gone, so you have more time to get home.
write one short plan without choosing the time i will leave the park.
use the other road, keep the walk home in mind, and leave enough time to return before you need to be home.
i know who asks about a person. what does whose ask about?
whose can ask about the person who has something as their own. for example: whose book is this?
give me just the meaning of that example.
whose book is this asks who has this book as their own.
if i answer my sister, is that enough?
it may be clear in a short conversation. you can also make it a full sentence: it is the book of my sister.
what question would my sister answer without being about a book?
who came to visit?
now ask whose with a garment on a chair.
whose garment is on the chair?
what if nobody knows yet?
you can say: we do not know whose garment it is.
can whose be used in a sentence that is not a question?
yes. the girl whose book i found came to the door.
explain that sentence with two simple sentences.
i found a book. the girl who had that book as her own came to the door.
does that tell us she lost the book before i found it?
not for sure. finding it does not tell us whether she lost it or knew where it was.
just give me an example with who and no book now.
the girl who came to the door is my sister.
my brother got home after a long trip. i want to send him a message that is warm, but i do not want to ask him many questions while he is tired.
welcome home. i hope you can have some quiet time after the long trip.
i also want him to know i would like to hear about it later.
you can add: i would like to hear about the trip when you feel ready to talk.
put those ideas together without making him choose a time now.
welcome home. i hope you can rest after the long trip. i would like to hear about it when you feel ready to talk.
he said he is happy to be home but still has work to finish. does that mean the trip was wrong for him?
no. being happy to be home does not tell us he should not have gone. he can enjoy a trip and also be happy when it is over.
can you write a reply about the things he said?
i hope the work goes well and you get some rest after it. it is good that you are happy to be home.
did he say he enjoyed the trip?
no. he said he was happy to be home and still had work to finish. he did not say whether he enjoyed the trip.
then keep the reply short and leave the trip out.
i hope the work goes well and you get some rest soon.
why is soon different from now?
soon leaves a little time open. now asks about this moment.
my task has eight pages. i read three this morning and two after lunch. how many have i read?
you have read five pages.
how many are left?
three pages are left.
my friend says there are five left because i read five. why is five not right for the pages left?
five is how many you have finished. three is how many you still need to read. those are different parts of the eight pages.
what if i read one more page now?
then you will have read six pages, with two left.
can i say i finished the task then?
not if the task is to read all eight pages. you would still have two to read.
what if the teacher only asked us to read six of the eight?
then reading six pages could finish the task. you still need to know whether the teacher asked for specific pages or any six pages.
what if the teacher chose the first six pages?
then you need to read the first six, not just any six pages. the number alone does not say which pages you read.
i read the first three, then the next two. now i read the next one. have i done the first six?
yes. three, then two, then one in that order makes the first six pages.
give me a short sentence i could tell the teacher.
i have read the first six pages.
does that tell the teacher i read all eight?
no. it says you read the first six, not the whole eight.
what is different between i cannot come and i do not want to come?
i cannot come says something stops you from coming. i do not want to come says coming is not what you want.
can both be true?
yes. you might not want to come, and you might also have something else that stops you.
what if i want to come but have to work?
then i cannot come because i have to work can make that clear. you can add that you would like to come if you want to share that too.
write it in a kind way in one sentence.
i would like to come, but i have to work.
does that have the word cannot in it?
no. it gives the reason without using cannot. if you want that word, you can say: i would like to come, but i cannot because i have to work.
now what if i am free but want a quiet evening at home?
then it is more clear to say that choice rather than give work as a reason.
write that without making it a long explanation.
thank you for asking, but i want a quiet evening at home.
can i still be kind if i do not give every reason?
yes. a short, clear answer can be kind without giving every detail.
end with a short message that is still useful.
thank you, but i will stay home this evening.
my teacher said to look at the picture on page three. should i read the whole page before answering?
what did the teacher ask you to find in the picture?
she asked what the child is holding.
then begin with the picture. you are looking for the object in the hands of the child, not every word on the page.
i can see a book, but i do not know whether it is a school book.
you can answer a book without adding school. the picture may show the object without making clear what kind of book it is.
give me just the answer.
the child is holding a book.
now the teacher asks where the child is standing. can i use that same answer?
no. holding a book answers what the child has in their hands. where asks for a place.
the child is by a window. answer the new question.
the child is standing by a window.
can you put both answers into one sentence?
the child is standing by a window and holding a book.
what if the words below the picture say the child is at school?
then the page gives you more information. you can say the child is standing by a window at school.
does that mean the book must be a school book?
not for sure. being at school does not tell us which kind of book the child is holding.
write a story about a woman looking for a key. use things that could happen in a real house, with no talking objects.

a woman was ready to leave for work when she could not find her key. she looked on the table by the door, then in the kitchen. it was not there. she sat down for a moment and thought about coming home the evening before. she remembered carrying a book and a warm garment into the bedroom. she went to look there and found the key on the shelf near the book. she took it, put the garment away, and left for work.
give me just the sentence where she finds the key.
she went to look there and found the key on the shelf near the book.
was the key on the kitchen table?
no. she looked in the kitchen, but found it on a shelf in the bedroom.
what helped her think of the bedroom?
she remembered carrying a book and a garment there when she came home the evening before.
does that mean every key will be in a bedroom?
no. it is where this key was in this story.
write the first sentence with i so i can tell it myself.
i was ready to leave for work when i could not find my key.
now use we and our instead.
we were ready to leave for work when we could not find our key.
is were right even though the first example had was?
yes. i was and we were are right for those examples.
finish with only the place where the key was found.
on the shelf near the book in the bedroom.
does even if there is rain, i will go mean there is rain now?
no. even if gives something possible. it says you plan to go with rain or without it, but it does not say rain is happening now.
give me the example and then one short sentence about the rain.
even if there is rain, i will go. that keeps rain as something possible, not something you know is happening now.
what if i say there is rain, but i will go?
then you are saying there is rain and you still plan to go.
can i keep the same place in both examples?
yes. for example, both can be about going to the library.
write those two full examples.
even if there is rain, i will go to the library. there is rain, but i will go to the library.
now make the first one about a friend coming instead of me going.
even if there is rain, my friend will come.
does that mean the friend is already here?
no. will come is about later, not a visit already happening.
now change will to may.
even if there is rain, my friend may come.
what changed?
may makes the visit less sure. the friend could come, but you are not saying it will happen for sure.
only tell me what did not change.
rain is still something possible in the plan.
i cleaned the kitchen, but the living room still needs work. can i say the house is clean?
that might sound as if the whole house is clean. it is more clear to say the kitchen is clean if that is the part you have finished.
my brother asks if he can start cooking. what should i tell him?
the kitchen is clean and ready for cooking.
did i tell you it is ready for cooking, or only that i cleaned it?
you only told me you cleaned it. there might be other things needed before cooking, so i should not add ready for cooking as a fact.
then write the answer with that part open.
the kitchen is clean. is there anything else you need before you start cooking?
he says he needs a pot, and it is still in the living room.
then getting the pot is one more thing to do before he can use it for cooking. cleaning the kitchen did not move the pot there.
write one short question i can ask him about help.
would you like me to bring the pot?
he says yes, please. i bring it. now what can i say?
here is the pot.
can i say the whole house is done now?
not from that. you said the living room still needs work, and bringing the pot does not mean that work is finished.
only give a sentence about what i have done.
i cleaned the kitchen and brought the pot.
i have a free evening. i could read or draw, and i like both. can you help me choose without calling one better for everyone?
what do you want from the evening: to follow a story, to make something, or simply to rest?
i want to make something, but i am tired.
then a small drawing could work for your goal. it would let you make something without choosing a large task.
why might a small drawing work?
you want to make something, but you are tired. a small drawing can let you do that without a large task.
what if i start drawing and want to stop?
you can stop. choosing a drawing does not mean you have to finish it this evening.
what if i want to finish it another day?
then you can leave it for another day. you do not have to choose between finishing it now and never finishing it.
can you give me three things i could draw using only objects already in my room: a cup, a book, and a chair?
you could draw the cup, the book, or the chair.
that just gives my words back. help me choose a small part to draw instead.
you could draw only the top of the cup, the open pages of the book, or one leg of the chair.
which one could have very few parts to draw?
the top of the cup may work if it looks like a simple circle from where you sit.
give me one thing to try first.
try the top of the cup as a simple circle, if that is how it looks from where you sit.
is i gave a book for my sister right?
if you mean she got the book from you, say i gave a book to my sister. if you mean you gave a book to someone else to help her, for my sister could be part of that different meaning.
i mean she got it from me. write the whole sentence with the.
i gave the book to my sister.
now make it shorter by putting my sister before the book.
i gave my sister the book.
are those two sentences about the same giving?
yes. both can say you gave the book and your sister got it.
what if she gave it back to me later?
you can say: my sister gave the book back to me later.
who has the book after that?
you do, if that was the last change of place.
now use her instead of my sister in the sentence about my first giving.
i gave her the book.
why not she?
in that sentence, she is the person getting the book, so use her. she works at the start of a sentence like she gave me the book.
is every sentence starting with her wrong?
no. her book is on the table starts with her and can be right. you need to look at how the word is used, not only its place.
give just that last correct example.
her book is on the table.
my cousin asked if i want to visit tomorrow. i do want to go, but i need to check with my mother first.
you could say: i would like to come tomorrow, but i need to check with my mother before i say yes for sure.
can you make it shorter and keep that i want to come?
i would like to come. i need to check with my mother first.
my cousin says okay, let me know later. does that mean i have to answer right now?
no. she has said you can tell her later. it would still be useful to answer when you know, rather than leave the plan open after you have chosen.
what if my mother says tomorrow does not work, but the next day does?
then you can tell your cousin tomorrow does not work and ask whether the next day is possible.
write the message without saying my cousin has to change her plan.
tomorrow does not work for me. would the next day work for you?
she says no, she is busy. what could i say without asking her to explain every detail?
okay. we can choose another day when we are both free.
does busy mean she never wants to see me?
no. being busy on one day does not tell us that. she may want to visit at another time.
only give the last message i could send.
okay. we can choose another day when we are both free.
help me use first, then, and finally in a plan for my morning. i want to eat breakfast, walk to the library, and return a book.
first, eat breakfast. then walk to the library. finally, return the book.
is finally saying the book return is the last thing in my whole life?
no. it is the last part of this small plan, not the last thing you will do in your life.
give that answer in fewer words.
it is the last part of this plan, not the last thing in your life.
what if the library is closed when i get there?
then the plan needs to change. you could return the book another time, but you would need to know when the library is open.
can you put if into the last part?
finally, return the book if the library is open.
does that say i should leave the book outside if it is closed?
no. it only says to return it if the library is open. it does not give a plan for leaving it outside.
now write the plan as what i will do rather than telling me to do it.
first, i will eat breakfast. then i will walk to the library. finally, i will return the book if the library is open.
what did you change to make it about my plan?
the plan now has i will to say what you plan to do.
make it one sentence with no finally.
i will eat breakfast, then walk to the library and return the book if it is open.
i told you i could not finish it. what should you ask before saying i need to study more?
what were you trying to finish?
a book, but it was not for school. i just did not enjoy it.
then studying more may not be the help you want. are you asking whether to keep reading, or do you want to talk about what you did not like?
i want to talk. i liked the first part, but then every person in the story left the town.
that sounds like the change in place and people changed what you enjoyed. what had you liked about the first part?
the people all knew each other. i liked the conversations in the shop.
so the town and the people talking together were important to you. when they left, the story no longer had that same feeling.
can you help me say that in a few sentences without saying i read the whole book?
i liked the first part of the book because the people knew each other and talked in the shop. after they left the town, i did not enjoy it as much. i have not finished the whole book.
what did those sentences keep clear about how much i read?
they say you have not finished the whole book. they are about the part you read.
now leave out the shop but keep the reason about people knowing each other.
i liked the first part of the book because the people knew each other. after they left the town, i did not enjoy it as much. i have not finished the whole book.
if someone just says yes, do you know what they said yes to?
not without the question or more context. yes can answer many different questions.
i asked whether my friend wanted tea, and she said yes.
then yes is an answer saying she wants tea.
now i ask whether she has already had lunch, and she says yes. is that still about tea?
no. it answers the new question about lunch.
can one word have a clear meaning because of the question before it?
yes. the question can give the context that makes a short answer clear.
what if i change her answer to not yet after the lunch question?
then she is saying she has not had lunch before now.
does that tell me she never wants lunch?
no. not yet leaves open having lunch later.
now i ask whether she wants to eat with me. she says maybe. what do i know?
she has not said yes or no for sure. eating together is still a possible plan.
should i tell another friend we are having lunch together for sure?
no. maybe is not a sure yes. you can say you asked, but the plan is not chosen yet.
give the short answer.
no. the plan is not chosen yet.
if she later says yes, i would like that, what changed?
now she has said yes to eating with you. you can choose the time and place together.
help me write about visiting my grandfather. i remember sitting in his kitchen and hearing a story about his first work in a shop. do not add the weather because i do not remember it.
i sat with my grandfather in his kitchen while he told me about his first work in a shop.
can you make it a little longer using only what i told you?
you have given the person, place, and what you heard. i can make those into two sentences, but more details would need more information from you.
show me those two sentences.
i visited my grandfather and sat in his kitchen. he told me about his first work in a shop.
what could you ask to get one more real detail?
what do you remember about the work he told you about?
he worked in a shop and liked talking to the people who came in.
then you could add: he worked in a shop and enjoyed talking to the people who came in.
can you keep liked as the word i gave you?
yes. i can keep liked so the sentence has your own word for how he felt.
put the whole thing together using liked.
i visited my grandfather and sat in his kitchen. he told me about his first work in a shop. he liked talking to the people who came in.
what did you not add?
i did not add the weather, an hour, or a name for the shop.
can you say there was snow outside?
no. you asked me not to add weather you do not remember.
i have enough to think about now. please do not give me a list of more things to do.
okay. we can stop here for now.
can you say something warm without saying i must come back?
i hope the rest of your day goes well.
what if i am going to bed soon?
then i can say: i hope you sleep well.
i am not asking for a sleep plan. just a short goodbye.
goodbye. i hope you sleep well.
now make it only three words.
sleep well. goodbye.
why did you put sleep before goodbye?
you asked for only three words, and that order keeps both the kind wish and the goodbye.
could goodbye. sleep well also work?
yes. goodbye. sleep well has the same three words in a different order.
then give me that one, with no explanation.
goodbye. sleep well.
